extracted.intended_audience: Heads of executive departments and establishments; agency managers responsible for workplace parking/transportation
extracted.subtask_description: A draft Office of Management and Budget circular proposing a federal policy for employee parking: establishing fees, carpooling requirements, and implementation guidance for Federal installations. It asks agencies to comment and to implement parking management measures (fees, carpool/vanpool plans, phase-in) to reduce subsidies and encourage transit and carpooling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish fees for use of Federal parking
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft circular intended to establish fees for the use of employee parking at Federal installations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document transmits a proposed pricing policy that agencies are asked to review and comment on; comments should be sent to Joyce Walker, Deputy Associate Director, OMB. The fee policy is the central proposed action of the circular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parking fee based on fair monthly rental value
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular would establish a parking fee at all Federal installations based on the fair monthly rental value of the parking space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee calculation should use the fair monthly rental value of the parking space as the basis. The intent is to use market rental value rather than ad hoc amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver threshold: no fee when rental value <$10/month
rubrics_metrics.description: In most cases no fee will be charged where the rental value is less than $10.00 per month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This threshold is intended to exempt very low-rent parking from charging; agencies should generally not charge when market rental value falls below the stated floor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee level objective: recover costs and incentivize carpooling
rubrics_metrics.description: The intent is to set a fee high enough to recover space costs and act as an incentive to carpooling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set fees to balance revenue recovery and behavioral incentive: sufficient to change behavior (increase carpooling/transit) while mindful of administrative feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid fees so low that administration consumes revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee should not be so low that administration of a fee system and parking management would totally consume the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When selecting fee levels and administrative arrangements, consider transaction/administrative costs so net benefit (in revenue or management outcome) remains positive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency managers to develop affirmative carpool/vanpool plans when parking remains free
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency manager at locations which would continue to provide parking without charge will be required to develop and implement affirmative plans for maximizing carpooling, vanpooling among employees, and other building tenants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an agency elects to continue providing free parking at a location, the agency must nevertheless implement concrete programs and plans to increase shared rides (carpool/vanpool) among occupants and tenants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase-in period to allow adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular provides for a phase-in period to help employees and agencies adjust carpooling and financial arrangements as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement fee changes gradually to allow time for employees to form carpools, change commuting arrangements, or otherwise adjust financially; agencies should plan transitions over the phase-in timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: More stringent application of carpooling requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: More stringent application of carpooling requirements will affect all locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveys show carpooling regulations were not uniformly applied; the circular calls for stricter enforcement/application of carpool rules to achieve higher carpool utilization (e.g., address single-occupant use of Government spaces where carpool targets exist).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary scope: downtown and densely populated suburban facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The pricing policy will primarily affect Federal facilities in downtown locations and densely populated suburban locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should prioritize implementation at high-demand urban cores and dense suburbs where market rental values and transit alternatives make pricing and demand-management most relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use commercial-equivalent fees to reduce demand (empirical support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies (e.g., Washington Metropolitan Area Council of Governments, Los Angeles study) indicate that charging commercial-equivalent fees for parking reduces automobile use and increases carpooling and transit usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The circular’s pricing approach is supported by empirical evidence that market-level parking prices reduce solo driving; agencies should consider local study evidence when setting fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected policy outcomes as success metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Considerable cost savings to the taxpayer, reduced energy consumption, less traffic congestion, increased transit use, greater carpooling and improved air quality are expected from this action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These outcomes function as policy goals/metrics against which implementation success can be judged; agencies should monitor and report on cost savings, mode-shift to transit/carpool, traffic/congestion effects, and air quality improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of employee hardship and mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: In the vast majority of cases, charging a commercial rate for parking is not expected to impose a hardship; employees may share costs through carpooling or choose public transit as cost-effective alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When implementing fees, consider potential hardship and provide mitigation via carpooling programs, transit resources, or the phase-in period; agencies should evaluate individual/location-specific burdens.
